## Serialized behind #17242 — ⛔ not deferred, and the reason is a file, not a doubt

Posted by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (session `session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`) at 2026-09-22T16:32Z, on selecting this card for dispatch. `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`, with `Blocked-by: #17242` added bare and line-leading at the top of the body so the unlock scan can grep it.

⭐ **This card is READY** — it is one of the best-specified in the lane. Scope is one sentence («give the two file-level `@example` blocks in `packages/spec/src/api/odata.zod.ts` a `<!-- os:check -->` line each and make them independently compilable»), the cost is pre-measured (the blocks need an `ODataQuery` import, and the generated reference page will move), and the acceptance test is two-sided: **strip a `$` and the gate must go RED; put it back and it must go GREEN** — ⛔ the green half alone does not count.

### The collision, measured rather than assumed

Card #17242's governing claim (`5777517463`, 2026-09-22T13:36Z) declares its surface as **comment prose in `packages/spec/src/**`**, minus 23 files it lists as held by in-flight PRs. Parsed that list: **23 files, and `api/odata.zod.ts` is not among them.** Its PR **#19733** is open (draft).

⇒ This card's whole deliverable is an edit to a docblock in `packages/spec/src/api/odata.zod.ts` — squarely inside that claim. The serial rule is 相交 ⇒ 排该 PR 之后串行或让行, and yielding is the cheaper half here: the marker lines are two edits, while re-deriving a citation corpus around someone else's concurrent edit is not.

⚠️ ⛔ This seat did **not** claim the file to make it "held" and so shrink #17242's surface from under it. That census was taken once, at claim time, and gaming it afterwards is not serialization — it is a race.

### What unblocks it

PR #19733 landing. A note is going on #17242 so that seat knows this rider exists; ⛔ nothing is asked of them beyond knowing.

⚠️ For whoever picks it up after: re-read the card's coverage numbers first. They were taken 2026-09-18T15:03Z on a tree that has moved a long way since, and the card says so itself.

### Why this is no longer blocked — the holder said so, ⛔ this seat did not infer it

This card was set `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: #17242` at 2026-09-22T16:31Z, because #17242's governing claim declares its surface as **comment prose in `packages/spec/src/**`** and `api/odata.zod.ts` is not among its 23 excluded files. That was the right call on the evidence then, and ⛔ this seat did not override it by reading the PR's file list.

What changed is **the holding seat's own written scope**, posted on #17242 at 2026-09-22T16:43Z and confirmed by its dev's report at 2026-09-22T17:25Z:

> Round 2 dispatched — the three fail bases, and ⛔ nothing else … all inside **the one file the PR already touches** (`scripts/check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors.mjs`) … **still 1 file**, now +269/−17.

And round 1's accepted substance inverted the card's own premise: the residual is a **spelling population, not rot**. ⇒ that round's work is the **gate**, not the prose, and PR #19733 has touched zero files under `packages/spec/src/**` across two rounds.

⭐ That is a statement of scope by the seat that holds the surface — better evidence than either a declared-surface reading or a file-list reading, and it is what releases this card rather than a judgment call by this seat.

⚠️ Recorded as a residual risk rather than waved away: a later round of #17242 could still reach `packages/spec/src/**` prose. The exposure here is **two marker lines and one import inside one docblock**, so a collision would be one hunk to merge, ⛔ not a re-derivation. The dispatch is told to keep the diff exactly that small.

### Serial check at 2026-09-22T18:20Z

Read against every in-flight `Claim:` in the lane, ⛔ not only this seat's own. `api/odata.zod.ts` appears in **no** other declared surface: #19580 (`integration/`), #19054 (`data/ conversions/ migrations/` + `authorable-surface/` + `json-schema/`), #17418 (`scripts/check-keyed-text-bounds.mjs`), #15178 (`system/translation.zod.ts`), #14512 (`stack.zod.ts`, `objectql/src/registry.ts`), #18682 (no declared surface — ⚠️ a half-state, so this seat also checked its subject: relationship-traversal predicates, ⛔ not odata). No open PR's actual file list touches `api/odata.zod.ts`.

`content/docs/references/api/odata.mdx` is `merge=os-regen`-routed ⇒ the dispatch carries the four-step sequence and the sibling-survival assertion.

## `pm:retriage` — this card's SCOPE sentence is falsified by measurement, and the residual is a three-way choice

Raised by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (session `session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`) at 2026-09-22T19:23Z. ⛔ Nothing else relabelled; the card stays `pm:dispatched` with its PR in flight, and `pm:retriage` rides beside it as the protocol allows. ⛔ The seat takes no position on the answer.

### What the card asks, and why it cannot be done as written

> 给 `packages/spec/src/api/odata.zod.ts` **文件级 docblock 的那两个** `@example` 块各加一行 `<!-- os:check -->`

**Only one of the two can carry that marker.** Measured by the seat at source, independently of the dev's report:

- `origin/main:packages/spec/scripts/check-skill-examples.ts:700` — `const FENCE_OPEN_RE = /^```(ts|tsx|typescript)\s*$/;`
- On the branch, the two fences are `:43` — a **bare** ``` opening an HTTP `GET /api/odata/customers?…` — and `:56` — ` ```typescript ` opening the `ODataQuery` literal.

The dev then ran the falsifier rather than arguing it: marker planted above the bare fence ⇒ **gate exit 1**, «Found an os:check marker not directly above a ts/tsx/typescript fence — `packages/spec/src/api/odata.zod.ts:43`».

⇒ ⭐ A marker on the second block does not merely fail to help — **it fails the gate**, and a file that fails the gate is worse than one outside it. The card's 「两个」 was written from a count of `@example` lines, ⛔ not from the fences. The ACCEPTANCE premise is untouched and was met in both directions (strip a `$` ⇒ RED with `TS2561` naming `$select`; restore ⇒ GREEN, 258→**259** blocks, spec-source surface 10→**11**).

### The residual, and why the seat is not choosing

`@example OData Query` ships — in the tarball and on the generated reference page — and is now the only one of the two outside any gate's reach. A TypeScript compiler **structurally cannot** read an HTTP request. Three shapes, quoted from the dev's report, ⛔ unranked by this seat:

- **A** — leave it unguarded and record why in the docblock. Its argument: the now-marked block pins the exact `$`-prefixed key spellings the URL block illustrates, so the defect class this card was opened for is already closed on the only surface a compiler can rule.
- **B** — teach `check-skill-examples` a fourth fence language, with its own non-tsc verdict. A new instrument and a new class of verdict, for a population of one today.
- **C** — rewrite the block as TypeScript. Changes what the page teaches, from «here is the wire format» to «here is how to build one».

⚠️ **B and C are decision-shaped** (a new instrument; changing what a published page teaches). **A is a narrowing of this card.** Which of those three it is decides whether this card closes on its PR or stays open — and that is the scope call an execution seat ⛔ does not make.

### What is asked of triage

1. Does the card close when PR #19745 lands, on the reading that its criterion is met for every block a compiler can hold?
2. Or does it stay open for the residual — and if so, does the residual belong here, in the decision box, or as its own card?

⚠️ The card's coverage numbers (7 marked files against 134 writing `@example`) were taken 2026-09-18T15:03Z and the tree has moved a long way; this PR moves that by one. ⛔ Re-read them before ruling on anything wider than this file.

## ⚠️ Correction to this seat's retriage note — option A's reasoning is MEASURED FALSE in part

Posted by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (session `session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`) at 2026-09-22T20:01Z, correcting its own comment `5782585327`. ⛔ The three options and the scope question are unchanged; what changes is the evidence under one of them.

### What this seat relayed, and why it needs correcting

The retriage note quoted the implementer's recommendation of **A** with its reasoning:

> the marked block now pins the exact `$`-prefixed key spellings the URL block illustrates, so **drift in one is visible in the other**

⛔ This seat passed that on **as stated** rather than measuring it. The at-tier review of PR #19745 (record `5783191138`) measured it, and it holds only in part:

| leg | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| the two blocks name the identical 7-key set (`$select $filter $orderby $top $skip $expand $count`), all in the schema | **survives** |
| «drift in one is visible in the other» | ⛔ **FALSE as a gate property** |
| the marked block pins what the URL block illustrates | ⛔ **only key NAMES, not the wire form** |

**The falsifier, measured:** misspell `$select=` as `select=` on line 45 — inside the URL block — and the gate stays **GREEN**, exit 0, 259 blocks / 11 on the spec-source surface. ⇒ the gate is blind to that block, so «visible in the other» is a claim about a **human** reading the two side by side, ⛔ not a mechanical pin.

**And a second gap:** the two blocks illustrate **different value encodings** — `$select=name,email` and `$expand=orders` as comma-strings in the URL, versus arrays in the TypeScript. Both are accepted by the schema's unions. So even the key-name overlap does not carry the wire form across.

### What this changes for the ruling — and what it does ⛔ not

⭐ **A still means «leave it unguarded and record why». It does ⛔ not mean «guarded by proxy».** That distinction is the whole of this correction: a ruling for A should be made knowing the URL block has **no** mechanical guard of any kind, ⛔ not on the belief that the marked sibling covers it.

⛔ This seat still takes no position between A, B and C, and B and C remain decision-shaped exactly as the retriage note said. ⚠️ The only thing that moved is that one argument for A is weaker than it was presented — by this seat, which relayed it without measuring it.

### Unchanged, and now with a PASS behind it

The scope sentence 「那两个 `@example` 块」 is falsified: a marker above the bare fence makes the gate **fail** (exit 1, «Found an os:check marker not directly above a ts / tsx / typescript fence — `odata.zod.ts:43`»). PR #19745 carries an at-tier **PASS** on head `4a5470603b`, is `mergeable_state: clean` with 33 success / 2 skipped / 0 failure, and is `Part of` — ⛔ it does not close this card. The two questions put to triage stand as written.
